title: Priority Lane round 3: dialogue options
about: This page offers three dialogue drafts for the whole of Priority Lane round 3 (about 14 s, beats A to D), synthesised from ten independent writers. Nothing has changed yet: no scene file, script or voice has been touched.

dialogues.label: Priority Lane round 3
dialogues.target: about 14 s total; spoken words 7-9 s max; last 3 s flatline with no words

now.line: BP 60 over 30, we're gonna lose him!
Come on, get out of the way!
[on the phone, crossing in front of the ambulance] I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

drafts.name: The quiet stop
drafts.bet: The picture and the silence do the outrage; fewer words make the minister's line the loudest thing in the short.

lines.line: BP 60 over 30, we're gonna lose him!
Get the f*** out of the way!
[no line: glove up, siren dies, rain, monitor beeping fast]
[on the phone, through the glass] I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

notes: Shape 02 spine; Kai's 'oxygen dropping' added back so the crew do not feel under-voiced. 'What's he doing?!' is cut: the glove asks it.
Protected lines kept verbatim. Risk: needs a tight monitor shot in A and the siren must drop out cleanly at the stop. Spare seconds are the breathing room.

drafts.name: The countdown
drafts.bet: Escalating real numbers and a stake ('two minutes out') make the stop cost something, and a cut-off figure lets the viewer finish the death themselves.

lines.line: BP 60 over 30! F***ing hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
Two minutes out! Get the f*** out of the way!
[muffled through the glass] I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[quiet, to the patient] Fifty over twen--
[flatline tone cuts the word; silence; black; logo]

notes: Trim first if tight: 'Two minutes out!'. 'Fifty over twen--' is a proposal for Jack and its numbers need a medical eye; if Suno smooths it, cut it in the edit.
Protected lines kept verbatim. Risk: heavy overlap may muddy the numbers; the last fragment may feel like one beat too many before the tone.

drafts.name: We can see it
drafts.bet: A visible destination makes the stop outrageous without any moral: the hospital is in the windscreen.

lines.line: BP 60 over 30, sats dropping, we're gonna lose him!
[bagging him, pointing forward] A&E's at the end of this road, go go go!
Get the f*** out of the way!
[the glove up] We can SEE it! It's right there!
[through the glass, crossing slowly] I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

notes: Shape 08. Needs the lit A&E sign in the windscreen still, or the lines lie. 'We can SEE it' is a new line, a proposal for Jack.
If Suno will not overlap lines 3 and 4, drop 'It's right there!'. 'Two minutes' was removed as unmeasured guesswork. Protected lines kept verbatim.

ranking.verdict: Best discipline. Trusts the picture, keeps the flatline silent, no invented medicine. Fails only by being thin: a crew who barely speak risk under-delivering Kai's ER drama.
'We can SEE it' states the outrage through geography, not a moral. Fails: runs long, and depends on a still we have not made.
Strongest ending (the viewer finishes the number). Fails: invented 'fifty over twenty', Suno may not cut mid-word, too much overlap under the minister.
Real craft logic, numbers falling. Fails: too many lines, 'hurry up' twice reads as filler, mush risk.
Good panic opening. Fails: '...Raspberry?' echo tells the joke and risks mocking the crew; arch delivery kills the heroes.
Right length, clean. Fails: drops all swearing and escalation, so the crew read polite; the driver's 'Move!' is too thin.
Cut-off sentences are real panic. Fails: invents 'ten minutes', relies on TTS honouring dashes, and the broken line states the point.
Clear stakes. Fails: the shouted sum ('four minutes') is not how paramedics talk and it argues the point aloud, which is the lecture we avoid.
Chorus idea is neat. Fails: five voices in one Suno track will blur, and the bystander and 'Is he on the phone?' hand-hold the joke.
Fails hardest: a crew that says 'Yes, sir' and 'Take your time, sir' kills the desperate heroes Kai asked for and states the moral through sarcasm.

questions.text: Swearing: keep Kai's full 'f***ing hurry up' and 'get the f*** out of the way', or does Suno's speech mode need a swapped word?
Should the crew speak at all during the held beat B (1A says no, 1B and 1C do)?
Are invented numbers acceptable ('two minutes out', 'fifty over twenty'), or must a clinician confirm every figure first?
1C needs the lit A&E sign visible in the windscreen still. Is that a shot we want?
Any new crew line is a proposal for Jack: which of 'We can SEE it!', 'Why have we stopped?!' and 'Fifty over twen--' does he want?
